note: Rounds 33 to 35: the attached document carries the shipment as the scorer prices it, and the mail states one figure differently, its dimensions changed to match. Each base is one of those requests: the mail as a template, the document's truth, and a wrong value per field. tools/document_conflicts.py renders every base with every wrong field, column order and file format; a right reading is always the document's.

bases.subject: Air freight quote: {origin} to {destination}
bases.body:
Hi there,

Hope your week’s going well! Could you send me an all-in price in EUR for the cheapest air freight option from {origin} to {destination} ({destination_name})? We’ll deliver the shipment to {origin} ourselves, and it’ll be ready on 2026-11-27.

It’s {pieces} pieces of furniture samples, with a gross weight of {weight_kg} kg and a total volume of {volume_cbm} cbm. Each piece measures {length} x {width} x {height} cm. I’ve attached our packing specification for reference.

Thanks for checking!

Thanks a lot and have a lovely day!
Petra Hofmann
Export Desk, Hofmann Textilwerk KG

known_gaps.pieces: the mail's piece count wins over the document's 'Total pieces'. Owner: Cost (pixel/agents/rfq/extract.py _cargo_sources).
known_gaps.destination: the mail's destination wins over the document's 'Destination airport'; we would quote the wrong lane. Owner: Cost (pixel/agents/rfq/extract.py _cargo_sources).
known_gaps.weight:weight_per_piece: a table weight per piece is not multiplied out, so the mail's total weight wins. Owner: Cost (pixel/agents/rfq/extract.py _cargo_sources).
known_gaps.weight:table_only: a document with only a table (no total lines) does not count: the mail's weight wins. Owner: Cost (pixel/agents/rfq/extract.py _cargo_sources).
known_gaps.volume:table_only: a document with only a table (no total lines) does not count: the mail's volume wins. Owner: Cost (pixel/agents/rfq/extract.py _cargo_sources).
